alignments.note: Opening waw takes the ASV's And (rule 14).

Construct noun rendered attributively (rule 28) keeps its own word border; the supplied determiner the joins the noun of the expression (rule 15), and the supplied for stating what this fronted nominal contributes belongs to that nominal under rule 33, since no preposition and no object marker stands on it. Competing reading: treat for as a topicalizing supply and mark it added under rule 16's as-for limit; rule 33 is preferred because a single supplied for before a bare nominal is exactly what that rule places.
Nomen rectum rendered attributively as western, following the ASV rather than imposing of (rule 28).
The apodosis waw of וְהָיָה is left unrendered; the verse's one And is the opening waw's (rule 14).
הָיָה + לְ recast as English have: the existential verb takes shall have, headed on have (rule 43).
The possessive לְ is left with no English by the have recasting (rules 40, 43).
Suffix takes the subject pronoun ye of the possessive recasting (rules 40, 43).
Article on הַיָּם takes the written the (rule 15).
Noun sea.
Agreement article on the attributive adjective: the phrase's single the is the noun's first article (rules 22, 47).
Adjective great.
Waw takes the written and (rule 14).
Absolute גְבוּל takes border with the supplied determiner the joining the noun's unit (rule 15).
Supplied possessive thereof, marked as an ASV addition: no suffix or other possessive morpheme stands in the phrase (rules 18, 30). The italic corroborates but does not decide (rule 7).
Demonstrative this.
Finite verb with its auxiliary, headed on the lexical verb be (rules 17, 24).
The לְ is left with no English where the ASV writes a bare possessive your for the suffix (rule 40).
Suffix realized by the possessive your (rules 18, 40).
Construct noun border; the rectum is rendered attributively (rule 28).
Nomen rectum rendered attributively as west (rule 28).

review_notes: The two supplied determiners (t003, t013) are placed on their nouns under rule 15; no article morpheme stands in either phrase.
The clause's one possessive recasting is read under rule 43 (הָיָה takes shall have, לְ unrepresented, suffix takes ye); the second לָכֶם is a bare possessive under rule 40.
